facts.content: Patient presents with a 3-day history of diarrhea with midline lower abdominal cramps and one episode of vomiting this morning.
facts.source_text: CC: 3-day diarrhea with midline lower abd cramps; 1x emesis this AM

facts.content: Patient reports frequent urges to have diarrhea, needing to use the toilet approximately every 10 minutes.
facts.source_text: Diarrhea: frequent urges; needs toilet ~q10 min

facts.content: Patient reports a sensation of incomplete evacuation with diarrhea.
Patient reports no blood in the diarrhea.
Abdominal pain is periumbilical and sub-umbilical, crampy, and mild with self-pressure.
facts.source_text: Abd pain: periumbilical/sub-umbilical, crampy; mild pain with self-press

facts.content: Abdominal pain is relieved by bowel movements and passing gas.
Patient reports nausea.
Patient vomited once after eating fruit this morning.
Patient reports the vomit was not bloody and that the red color was from strawberries.
Patient has decreased oral intake and is likely under-hydrated.
Patient denies fever but reports night sweats and is unsure about a low-grade fever.
facts.source_text: Fever: denies; reported night sweats; unsure low-grade fever

facts.content: Patient has a history of asthma and is using an inhaler.
Patient reports no change in baseline shortness of breath.
Patient reports no chest pain.
Patient is unable to work due to frequency of stools and is staying home.
facts.source_text: SH: Staying home; unable to work due to stool frequency

facts.content: Acute gastroenteritis or foodborne illness is diagnosed, characterized by three days of non-bloody diarrhea, periumbilical cramps, and one episode of vomiting with a stable course.
facts.source_text: 1) Acute gastroenteritis/foodborne illness  3 days non-bloody diarrhea, periumbilical cramps, 1x emesis; stable course

facts.content: The patient is assessed to be at risk for dehydration due to decreased oral intake and high stool frequency.
facts.source_text: 2) Dehydration risk   PO intake with high stool frequency

facts.content: The patients asthma is assessed as stable with no acute exacerbation despite an inhaler brand change.
facts.source_text: 3) Asthma  stable; inhaler brand change; no acute exacerbation

facts.content: The patient has health anxiety related to a family history of malignancy and was reassured that current symptoms are more consistent with infection.
facts.source_text: 4) Health anxiety re FHx malignancy  reassured; current sx more c/w infection

facts.content: For presumed gastroenteritis, patient is advised to increase oral fluid intake.
Patient is advised to monitor for fevers.
Patient is advised to stay home until symptoms are improving.
Antibiotics are to be avoided for the current gastroenteritis episode.
If symptoms worsen or do not improve over the next 1 to 2 days, the patient should arrange an in-person GP review for an abdominal exam.
facts.source_text:  #1/2 Follow-up: If worsening or not improving over next 12 days, arrange in-person GP review for abd exam

facts.content: Asthma management plan notes that the inhaler is unlikely to be the cause of gastrointestinal symptoms and that there are no reported respiratory red flags.
facts.source_text:  #3 Asthma: Inhaler unlikely cause of GI sx; no respiratory red flags reported
